name: MS-03
label: Safe R

Incumbent Guest has a large financial edge ($962K vs $23K cash on hand)

model.rationale: Guest combines a solidly Republican seat, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising advantage, while prediction markets price his win at roughly 98 percent. The Democratic challenger has raised little and no polling suggests competitive conditions.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or outside spending surge for the challenger could narrow the race, though nothing currently signals that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Michael Guest, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a Mississippi district that leans Republican by about fourteen points. He has built a substantial financial advantage, holding nearly a million dollars on hand, while Democratic challenger Michael Chiaradio has raised modest sums and has little cash remaining. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets price Guest's chances at roughly 98 percent. The fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent win, with the main uncertainty being how strongly the national environment moves voters in a district that has favored Republicans consistently.
